source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-19:10 (tools/video_draft.py transcript 7YcSZYPLge8 --start 0 --end 1150); nothing past 19:10 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches. Solo draft: every idea is the host's (speaker field kept for the schema).

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Kiora of Fire and Ashes is completely messed up; it is chosen over Vraska, the Cutting Glare, a gold uncommon that might wheel, and with six mana he would rather play Kiora.
ideas.quote: Kiora is so good though. It's like really, really good.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Kiora of Fire and Ashes against Vraska, the Cutting Glare.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A rule not to pass Mindseeker Oculus: you can break it but you need a really good reason.
ideas.quote: I have a rule, don't pass Mind Seeker Oculus. You can break rules sometimes but you really should have a really good reason to do that.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Mindseeker Oculus.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Arni, Humble Scribe has been a journey card for him: he started really high on it, went much lower, then came back; Extended Absence is better.
ideas.quote: Arni was a journey card for me. I started off really high on it, then I went really much lower on it, then I came back on it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Arni, Humble Scribe.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Extended Absence is really strong and easily splashed a lot of the time; he takes it over Twinned Vision, which he would not third-pick.
ideas.quote: Very easily to splash a lot of the time.
ideas.test_idea: Splash win rate of Extended Absence.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Blue-black with Kiora: you can sometimes splash double red cards in this format.
ideas.quote: Blue black with a Kiora. You can sometimes splash double red cards in this format.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of splashed double-pip cards.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A couple of colourless cards help you delay the colour decision, which is a good term sometimes: the longer you can wait the more you can get from a signal like a seventh-pick great card.
ideas.quote: Getting a couple colorless cards just helps you delay the decision.
ideas.test_idea: Final-colour agreement by number of colourless picks in pack 1.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Vraska did not wheel: someone took the green-black Vraska and the Jeskai one, a sign those colours are being drafted by the players upstream.
ideas.quote: We wheel Vraska. No. Good to know. So, somebody took the green black Vraska.
ideas.test_idea: Wheel rate of gold uncommons in packs with two gold uncommons.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A land over a mediocre playable when playables are plentiful: Transformative Commons over Hallway Heckler; he just likes taking lands when he sees them in weird spots.
ideas.quote: I just like taking lands when I see them in weird spots.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of lands taken at picks 9-11.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is much easier to splash than a double-blue card like Chandra, Chill of Compliance; Murmuring Volume is his favourite card in the set right now and he hates passing it.
ideas.quote: I hate passing Murmuring Volumes. It's like my favorite card in the set right now.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment against Chandra, Chill of Compliance; Murmuring Volume ALSA.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Samut, Hazoret's Champion is still a good card even if he is not aggressive: giving all his stuff haste after Kiora makes a real threat, and it is good against slow match-ups.
ideas.quote: Giving all your stuff haste is like you play your Kiora, Fire and Ashes, and all of a sudden you have a real threat on them.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Samut, Hazoret's Champion.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Face Yourself is a card he wants to play even outside Empower Jace: good with his legendaries; he takes it over Room of Refuge.
ideas.quote: I really want to play face yourself a bit. Feel like it could be good in this deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Face Yourself.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Land over the card made for his deck: Stingerquill Annex over Stingerquill Charm (three damage to anything), because he already has five removal spells and the land fixes both splashes.
ideas.quote: The land is going to be really helpful for this blue splash and this green splash is getting my mana more consistent.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Stingerquill Charm; play rate of Stingerquill Annex.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Craftwork Crusher is fine at pick eight and a second one at pick eight in pack three: 'oh my gosh'; the red-green uncommon appears late.
ideas.quote: Another crusher pick eight. Oh my gosh.
ideas.test_idea: Average pick position of Craftwork Crusher.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Murmuring Volume is so good it helps with every splash, gives every colour and ramps toward the big cards; he prefers it to a red-green land.
ideas.quote: Murmuring volume is so good. It just helps with every splash, gives me every color, and ramps me towards my big stuff.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Murmuring Volume by number of colours.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Plenty of playables already, so take the land: Formidable Commons over Stingerquill Charm; the count is 18 playables after two packs and he needs five more.
ideas.quote: I'm going to have plenty of playables here, like just looking at this deck.
ideas.test_idea: Playables at pick one of pack 3 and final win rate.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Twinned Vision in a red-base deck splashing blue: flashing it back is easy; Keeper of the Quiet Hour is also good but he likes having one.
ideas.quote: We are playing red base and splashing blue so it should be pretty easy to splash back the card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twinned Vision in decks with a blue splash.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Hungering Puppetbeast is a brilliant card: play it next turn, play Grapple with the Past with the bent mana, even though it is another double-green card.
ideas.quote: Puppet Beast is just a brilliant card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Hungering Puppetbeast.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Free-slot lands: he would take a 3/2 here, but because he took lands earlier he has plenty of playables, so Innovative Commons.
ideas.quote: These lands in like freebie slots like I would be taking like a 3-2 here, but because we took these earlier we have plenty of playables.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of dual lands taken at pick five of pack three.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Pack 3 pick 7 and 8: another Hapatra and another Crusher; with 18 lands in a deck of expensive cards.
ideas.quote: We're just going to place I think 18 lands in this deck.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of 17 vs 18 lands in decks with many 5+ drops.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: The blue might not be necessary: Recursive Recruitment is so good and he has lands for it, so he cuts the Oculus and plays it off three sources; he cuts Samut, Paradox Shaper and Heartstring Puller for an extra land.
ideas.quote: So maybe we'll cut the Oculus and just play this off of one, two, three sources and not play any basics for it.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of light splashes with only land sources.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Source counts for an 18-land three-colour-plus deck: seven to eight black, six to eight red, five to six green (with one land cut); 'my mana is kind of bad, that's okay'.
ideas.quote: Six, seven, eight black sources, six, seven, eight red sources, four, five green sources.
ideas.test_idea: Source counts against win rate in splash decks.
